title: Evaluating Domain Specific LLMs for Real World Finance — Waseem Alshikh, Writer
talk_summary: Writer's CTO built an open-source financial-domain benchmark (FinQA-style) that injects query failures (misspellings, incomplete, out-of-domain) and context failures (missing context, OCR errors, irrelevant context) to test whether models actually ground answers in provided context. They found thinking/reasoning models score well on answerability but degrade badly on grounding — up to 50-60% worse — and even the best model only reaches ~81% on robustness+context grounding, concluding you need full-stack guardrails, not just a better model.

takeaways.what_they_do: They built an eval that deliberately corrupts the input context (missing context, OCR errors, irrelevant documents) and separately corrupts the query (misspellings, incomplete, out-of-domain) to measure grounding vs. answerability independently.
takeaways.numbers: Best model only ~81% on robustness+context grounding; thinking models 50-60% worse on grounding

takeaways.technique: Score grounding separately from answer correctness
takeaways.what_they_do: They use two eval metrics: can the model answer, and does it follow the grounding/context. Models that look great on the first fail the second.
takeaways.evidence_quote: can the model actually give good follow to the grounding or context grounding

takeaways.technique: Don't assume bigger/thinking models are better for grounded tasks
takeaways.what_they_do: Their data shows reasoning/thinking models overthink and perform worse on context-grounding tasks than smaller models.
takeaways.evidence_quote: smaller model actually performing better than all this model overthinking at that side

takeaways.what_they_do: They test whether the model notices the provided document is completely irrelevant and refuses, rather than answering from the wrong context.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you end up basically uploading completely wrong document does lm going to still answer

takeaways.what_they_do: They conclude no single model is reliable enough and you need the surrounding system — grounding, guardrails, retrieval — to get reliability.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you need full stack you need the rock system you need the grounding you need everything from guard rails
takeaways.numbers: ~20% of requests still wrong at best
